skill.name: debug-tauri
skill.description: Guides local Tauri WebView debugging with screenshot capture, console log analysis, process checks, and structured debug reports.
skill.summary: Debug Tauri WebView apps with local screenshots, logs, process checks, and report templates.
skill.author: 8beeeaaat

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples or local debug helpers, not evidence of malware. I found no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or screenshot upload path, but the skill intentionally captures screenshots, reads local logs, and inspects app processes. Publish only with clear privacy warnings and local-only handling of collected artifacts.

remediation.issue: Screenshot capture can expose sensitive UI data.
remediation.suggestion: Limit capture to the target app window, require user approval, and redact screenshots before sharing.

remediation.issue: Legacy shell helpers use platform commands and shared temp files.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer official Tauri plugins and write artifacts to app-owned directories with restrictive permissions.

remediation.issue: Log analysis may include sensitive tokens, paths, or personal data.
remediation.suggestion: Filter or redact logs before AI review and avoid uploading collected artifacts.

remediation.issue: Shell helpers accept app names and bundle IDs from environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Validate identifiers, quote all paths, and reject values with path separators or traversal.

semantic_findings.title: Privacy-Sensitive Visual Capture
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents capture of all windows, primary monitors, and legacy screenshots for debugging. This is disclosed and local, but it can collect sensitive UI data if used outside a test app.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The screenshot reference explicitly includes all-window and monitor capture APIs, and the helper script invokes screenshot capture. No upload is shown, so the risk is local privacy exposure.

semantic_findings.title: Local Logs May Contain Sensitive Data
semantic_findings.description: The workflow collects frontend and backend logs and analyzes local log files. Logs can contain tokens, file paths, personal data, and application secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill describes automatic console collection and platform log files, while the analyzer script reads those logs. Sensitive contents depend on the target app, so the confidence is high but not absolute.

content.user_title: Debug Tauri WebViews with Local Evidence
content.value_statement: Tauri WebView failures can hide across process state, console logs, screenshots, and plugin permissions. This skill organizes local diagnostics into a focused workflow and report.
actual_capabilities: Verifies whether a target Tauri app process is running.
Guides screenshot capture with official Tauri screenshot plugins and legacy helpers.
Finds and analyzes Tauri plugin log files across supported platforms.
Collects WebView state such as URL, title, user agent, and viewport.
Structures findings into a repeatable debug report template.
limitations: Requires a Tauri app with compatible debug plugins or legacy platform tools.
Screenshots and logs can contain sensitive local information.
Legacy screenshot scripts are macOS focused and deprecated.
It diagnoses symptoms but does not automatically modify application code.

use_cases.title: Investigate WebView startup failures
use_cases.description: Check process status, visible UI state, console errors, and WebView metadata after a failed launch.

use_cases.title: Triage desktop UI regressions
use_cases.description: Capture a reproducible visual state and pair it with recent warnings, errors, and runtime details.

use_cases.title: Prepare focused debugging context
use_cases.description: Turn local logs, screenshots, and process checks into a concise report for root cause analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic Tauri check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debug-tauri workflow to verify my Tauri app is running and list the first evidence I should collect.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze local debug evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my screenshot observations and recent Tauri logs. Identify likely UI, runtime, or permission issues.

prompt_templates.title: Create a structured debug report
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my process status, WebView state, screenshot notes, and log findings into a Tauri debug report.

prompt_templates.title: Plan plugin migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess my current debug setup and propose a migration plan from legacy scripts to official Tauri plugins.

output_examples.input: A Tauri app opens a blank window after login.
output_examples.output: The report highlights a running process, missing WebView title, recent console errors, and next checks for permissions and initialization.

output_examples.input: A screenshot shows broken layout after resizing.
output_examples.output: The analysis links the visual issue to viewport data, recent warnings, and a short list of likely CSS or state causes.

output_examples.input: A team wants to replace legacy screenshot commands.
output_examples.output: The migration summary lists required plugins, capability changes, validation steps, and risks to test on each platform.

best_practices: Capture only the target app window when possible.
Redact screenshots and logs before sharing them with any external system.
Record process status, logs, screenshot notes, and WebView state in one report.
anti_patterns: Do not upload raw screenshots without reviewing visible data.
Do not rely on deprecated legacy scripts when official plugin APIs are available.
Do not treat empty logs as proof that no runtime error occurred.

faq.question: Does this skill require a running Tauri app?
faq.answer: Yes. Most checks need a running app process and configured debug or logging plugins.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots automatically?
faq.answer: It guides screenshot capture through official plugins and legacy helpers. Review screenshots before sharing them.

faq.question: Does it upload logs or screenshots?
faq.answer: No upload path was found in the skill. Users still need to control where collected artifacts are shared.

faq.question: Which platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The documentation covers macOS, Windows, and Linux through official Tauri plugins, with legacy macOS commands noted.

faq.question: Can it fix application bugs directly?
faq.answer: No. It organizes evidence and suggests likely causes, but code changes remain a separate step.

faq.question: What data should users protect?
faq.answer: Protect screenshots, console logs, process details, file paths, tokens, and any personal data shown by the app.
